parsed.explanation: No trans-specific offence, and no documented visitor-facing universal exposure (no bathroom/facility ban, no birth-sex custody rule, no border screening rule, no police campaign against gender-nonconforming people) — so this sits well above the institutional-exclusion dossiers. But the negatives are real: a live same-sex criminal statute with no documented enforcement against trans people (a secondary signal only), absolutely no recourse machinery (LGBTI groups cannot register, no anti-discrimination law, closed civic space in an absolute monarchy), documented societal stigma and two anti-LGBT killings in 2015, and policy inclusion sitting beneath unchanged criminal law. Offsetting positives: police-escorted Pride with ~2,000 attendees, an incident-free 2021 virtual Pride, a welcoming church, and 2021 health guidelines naming gender identity. Border treatment, ward and custody placement remain undocumented open questions. Deriving from the rubric: a latent tangential statute plus thin recourse plus open questions — a step below acceptance-with-working-remedies, not a tier below.
